lines.text: Driver! Motor park. Turn left.
I mean left. Emotionally.
Only one person ever laughed at page nine.
'Left. Emotionally.'
At our wedding the ram escaped. The imam caught it.
Lula-and-Faty, which of us is telling this?
Faty, write that down.
'We were there.' Put that. …She put that.
Ah! The young driver! Turn left to greet me. Emotionally.
Barka da yamma! [Good evening!] Faty, look who it is.
You again. Sit. I have a story. Faty, which story?
Go well. Turn left at the gate. I mean right. Ask Faty.
Thank you. Faty, write down that somebody thanked me.
You drive like I did. Before the ram. After the imam.
You call that a joke? Faty, is it a joke? …She says no.
Left. …Not that left. The other one. The emotional one.
Take your time. I took twenty years to find the market. Faty found it first.
Follow me. I know a shortcut. …Faty, where is the shortcut?
Pardon? Faty hears for both of us. Faty?
Who? There was nobody there fa. Only Faty, and she's always there.
Yes! Faty, I said yes. Write it down before I change.
No. Faty says no. So, no. Emotionally, maybe.
Have you written anything down today? Write it down. It goes.
A man asks for directions. His wife gives them. That's marriage.
Heat. In my day we had the same heat. Fewer fans. More stories.
Rain. Faty says it will stop. It will stop when Faty says.
Mama Nkechi's tuwo. Forty years I've eaten it. Forty years she says 'Again?'
For us? Faty, a gift! Write it down. Page… not nine. Somewhere.
A pen! A good pen! For the book! Faty, we have a pen now!
Faty, which of us said that? …Me? Good.
Forty-one years married. Forty jokes. One a year. We're behind.
At night we read the book. Out loud. Some pages twice.
Turn left. Emotionally. Still the best thing I ever said.
You won the Grand Prix. Or you stopped to help. Faty wrote down which.
Page nine? Ask Faty. …Don't ask Faty.
You still drive like the trophy is chasing you.
'Left. Emotionally.' Faty put it on my back. In chalk. I wore it to the market.
The sign-out party. Somebody wrote on my back. I know it was Faty.
You still visit old people. Good. We have the best gist.
At our wedding the ram escaped. The imam caught it. I told it on stage!
The open mic. I'm famous now. Faty's mother would be shocked.
Strike. The young ones left. We stayed. We always stay.
This year's joke? Not yet. Faty is very strict.
Still single? Faty and I met at a bus stop. Wrong bus. Right wife.
You have grown. Faty says so. I say so. Twice is a fact.
Market day. Faty bargains. I carry. I also bargain. Badly.
That night, Faty made me write the date. My hand shook. It's in.
We were there. It's in the book. In ink. Faty doesn't use ink.
The book is nearly full. We'll start another. On page one. Not nine.
Convocation. Turn left at the stadium. Faty, tell them which left.
Freshers! Every year they look younger. Faty says we look older.
Goal! Faty, write it! …She says a goal is not a joke. It is today.
Elections. I vote for whoever Faty votes for. Then I pretend I chose.
Convocation. Gowns everywhere. We'll write your name in the book. Not page nine.
Ramadan. Faty breaks fast with dates. I break fast with tea. Then dates.
Christmas. Our neighbours bring rice. We bring a joke. Fair trade.
Valentine's. I bought Faty a pen. Forty-one years. She still uses it.
Harmattan. My knees know before the radio does.
